drivingQuestion: Does the prohibition of the sciatic nerve apply to a non-kosher animal?
outcomeNote: The mishna records the dispute; the Sages have the last word but no decision is stated in this unit.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ נוֹהֵג בִּטְהוֹרָה, וְאֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג בִּטְמֵאָה. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף בִּטְמֵאָה. אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: וַהֲלֹא מִבְּנֵי יַעֲקֹב נֶאֱסַר גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה, וַעֲדַיִין בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה מוּתֶּרֶת לָהֶן? אָמְרוּ לוֹ: בְּסִינַי נֶאֱמַר, אֶלָּא שֶׁנִּכְתַּב בִּמְקוֹמוֹ.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» The prohibition of eating the sciatic nerve «applies to a kosher» animal «and does not apply to a non-kosher» animal. «Rabbi Yehuda says:» It applies «even to a non-kosher» animal. «Rabbi Yehuda said» in explanation: «Wasn’t the sciatic nerve forbidden for the children of Jacob,» as it is written: “Therefore the children of Israel eat not the sciatic nerve” (Genesis 32:33), «yet» the meat of «a non-kosher animal was still permitted to them?» Since the sciatic nerve of non-kosher animals became forbidden at that time, it remains forbidden now. The Rabbis «said to» Rabbi Yehuda: The prohibition «was stated in Sinai, but» it «was written in its place,» in the battle of Jacob and the angel despite the fact that the prohibition did not take effect then.

moves.summary: the anonymous mishna: the prohibition applies to kosher animals only
moves.about: the prohibition was in fact stated at Sinai and merely written in the narrative of its occasion, so nothing follows from the era of Jacob's sons

moves.summary: R' Yehuda dissents: it applies to non-kosher animals too
moves.about: whether the prohibition of the sciatic nerve applies to a non-kosher animal as well as to a kosher one

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי יהודה: והלא מבני יעקב נאסר גיד הנשה
moves.summary: argues from the era of Jacob's sons, when non-kosher meat was still permitted
moves.about: the sciatic nerve was already forbidden in the days of Jacob's sons, when non-kosher animals were still permitted to them — so the prohibition must have taken hold in non-kosher animals too

moves.summary: the prohibition was stated at Sinai and only written in its narrative place
